sections.h2: What is Washington County, Illinois, and who handles its property tax?
sections.html:
Washington County sits in the southern part of Illinois, about 564 square miles with Nashville as the county seat and largest city. The county was formed on January 2, 1818, out of St. Clair County, and the Kaskaskia River runs along its northern edge. Property tax here runs through two offices at the courthouse at 101 E. St. Louis Street in Nashville.

  • The Treasurer and Collector prepares and mails the bills, takes payments and runs the delinquent sale. The office answers at (618) 327-4800, extension 315, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • The Supervisor of Assessments handles the assessment side and works with the Board of Review. Call (618) 327-4800, extension 166.
  • The County Clerk and Recorder office records the deed when a house changes hands.

Six school districts serve the county: Oakdale CCSD 1, West Washington County CUD 10, Irvington CCSD 11, Ashley CCSD 15, Nashville CCSD 49 and Nashville Community High School District 99. Which district your parcel sits in decides a large share of the bill, so check the parcel before you quote a number to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do Washington County home values and ownership compare?
sections.html:
Washington County is small and heavily owner-occupied, with a value level well under the Illinois suburbs. Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 put the median owner-occupied home at $155,700 and the owner-occupancy rate at 84.1%.

The population has drifted down from 14,716 in 2010 to 13,761 in 2020. Only 15 building permits were issued in 2025, so little new construction competes with an existing house. Owner costs without a mortgage run $612 a month, and a share of that is the tax bill.

sections.h2: When are Washington County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Washington County bills real estate tax in two installments, and the dates change each year. For the 2025 taxes payable in 2026, the Treasurer mailed the bills on July 23, 2026, and the release set the first installment for September 11, 2026 and the second for October 16, 2026. The total to be collected that year was $32,673,520.80.

The county enforces those installment dates, and a postmark on a mailed payment counts. A bill that arrives late, or never arrives, does not change what you owe. Ask the Treasurer for a copy if you did not get one, or print it from the parcel lookup the office links on its page.

Mobile homes follow a separate cycle. Their bills go out in April and are due June 30, with a penalty of $25.00 per month that stops at $100.00. Unpaid mobile home tax turns into a lien filed on the home at the end of the calendar year, and these bills cannot be paid online.

sections.h2: How do you pay Washington County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by mail, in the Treasurer's office or in the courthouse drop box. The drop box sits at the south entrance on E. St. Louis Street, and cash never goes in it.

  • Mail the stubs with a check payable to the Washington County Treasurer, 101 E. St. Louis Street, Nashville, IL 62263.
  • Stub 1 pays the first installment, stub 2 the second, and both stubs together pay the full year at once.
  • Partial payments are refused, and a payment is void if the check or card fails to clear.
  • Add a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want a receipt back.

The county's 2026 release also named December 18, 2026 as the last day to pay online, by personal check or by business check. After that date the office takes only cash, a bank cashier's check or a money order.

sections.h2: What happens when Washington County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
A missed installment starts costing money right away. The Treasurer's page says a penalty of 1 1/2% per month applies after each due date, and the interest dates are printed on the stubs. The state tax code says the same rate runs in a county of fewer than 3,000,000 residents (35 ILCS 200/21-15).

Taxes still open after the books close go to the delinquent tax sale. The county's 2026 release listed that sale for Friday, January 22, 2027. A buyer at that sale gets a tax lien, and the owner keeps the right to redeem. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-350, property sold at a tax sale may be redeemed any time before three years from the date of sale, with the statute carving out exceptions, so ask the Treasurer which period applies to a given parcel.

For a seller, the practical point is simple: an unpaid installment sits on the property and grows each month. Get the payoff figure from the Treasurer before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How do assessment appeals work in Washington County?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the county Board of Review, and the clock is short. Under 35 ILCS 200/16-55, a complaint about the current year's assessment must be filed within 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published. It has to be in writing, and mail counts as filed on its postmark date.

The Supervisor of Assessments office at the courthouse also serves as the contact for the Board of Review, using the same (618) 327-4800 line, extension 166. Call before the window opens so you know when the list is published for your township.

A strong appeal compares your house with similar sales nearby rather than arguing that the tax is too high. A lower assessed value is the outcome you are asking the board for. Photos, a recent appraisal and sales of comparable homes make the case.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can reduce a Washington County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three state exemptions matter most for a Washington County homeowner. Because Washington County does not border a county of 3,000,000 or more residents, the lower dollar caps apply.

  • General homestead exemption: up to $6,000 off the equalized assessed value of an owner-occupied home, under 35 ILCS 200/15-175.
  • Senior citizens exemption: up to $5,000 for an owner who is 65 or older, under 35 ILCS 200/15-170.
  • Low-income senior assessment freeze: holds the assessed value at a base year for eligible seniors, under 35 ILCS 200/15-172. Ask the assessment office for the current income limit and the application period.

When a homestead is sold, the exemption stays in place for the rest of that assessment year, and the assessor may require the new owner to apply for the next year.

sections.h2: What should a Washington County owner do before selling with tax due?
sections.html:
Start with the Treasurer. Ask for the open balance on the parcel, including any penalty, and whether a delinquent amount has already gone to the January sale.

  • Pull the parcel number from the tax bill so the lookup finds the right record.
  • Settle the open installment out of the sale proceeds, and have the closing agent confirm the figure in writing.
  • Check whether a homestead or senior exemption is on the bill and tell the buyer the new owner may need to reapply.
  • Record the new deed with the County Clerk and Recorder once the sale closes.

An inherited house or one with a tenant adds steps, because the person who signs the deed has to be the owner of record. Sort that out before the buyer's title work, since a lien from unpaid tax can delay the closing.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The county bills in two installments each year. In 2026 the first was due September 11 and the second October 16. Ask the Treasurer at (618) 327-4800, extension 315, for the dates on your bill, because they change from year to year.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to a late Washington County payment?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page lists 1 1/2% per month once an installment is past due, and the stubs print the interest amounts. State law at 35 ILCS 200/21-15 sets the same monthly rate for a county under 3,000,000 residents.

faqs.q: Can I pay Washington County taxes online?
faqs.a: Real estate tax can be paid online through the parcel lookup the Treasurer links, so ask the office which payment types it takes. Mobile home tax cannot be paid online, and cards are not accepted for it. The 2026 release said personal and business checks and online payments stop being accepted after December 18, 2026.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Washington County assessment?
faqs.a: File a written complaint with the Board of Review within 30 calendar days after the assessment list is published (35 ILCS 200/16-55). Call the Supervisor of Assessments at (618) 327-4800, extension 166, for the form and the township schedule.

faqs.q: Do I need to clear unpaid tax before selling in Washington County?
faqs.a: The balance has to be dealt with before or at closing, because it stays attached to the parcel. Get a payoff from the Treasurer, pay it from the proceeds, and record the new deed with the County Clerk and Recorder.
